title: climateBR: An R package to download meteorological data from Brazil
text: climateBR supports research climate shocks providing functions stage working climate data: download_inmet() downloads ZIP files INMET weather station data Brazilian government’s website. build_inmet_dataset() converts raw files partitioned dataset. read_inmet() reads filters dataset. nearest_stations() kriging_inmet() link municipalities INMET stations, climate data can merged sources, IBGE TSE, statistical analysis. vignette demonstrates core workflow climateBR. package originated project Data Analysis course Graduate Program Political Science Federal University Pernambuco (UFPE). INMET functions procedure linking municipalities nearest weather stations developed preprint: Barbara, K. R., & Leite, D. . (2026). chuva diminui o comparecimento eleitoral? Evidências de eleições nacionais e municipais Brasil [Preprint]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23618763

title: Spatial Interpolation Using Ordinary Kriging
text: Spatial interpolation commonly used estimate meteorological variables locations direct observations available. kriging_inmet() function implements ordinary kriging using weather station observations spatial prediction locations provided sf objects. vignette demonstrates interpolate accumulated rainfall INMET weather stations.
code: library(climateBR) library(dplyr) library(sf) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork)

title: Spatial Interpolation Using Ordinary Kriging
text: example uses rainfall observations 2024 Rio Grande Sul flood event together municipality geometries. station observations converted sf object projected planar coordinate reference system, required distance-based spatial analysis.
code: data("floods_rs") data("mun_stations")  # Alternative to: geobr::read_municipality(year = 2024) tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".rda") on.exit(unlink(tmp), add = TRUE)  download.file(   "https://github.com/kaiorb52/dados_municipais/raw/main/mun_24.rda",   destfile = tmp,   mode = "wb" )  load(tmp) rain_sf <- floods_rs |>   st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>   st_transform(crs = 29193)  mun_centroid <- mun_24 |>   select(code_muni, geom) |>   mutate(     ponto = st_point_on_surface(geom)   ) |>   st_drop_geometry()  mun_grid_sf <- mun_centroid |>   st_as_sf() |>   st_transform(crs = 29193)

title: Spatial Interpolation Using Ordinary Kriging
text: kriging_inmet() function computes empirical variogram, fits spherical variogram model, performs ordinary kriging predictions target locations. predicted values (var1.pred) prediction variances (var1.var) attached municipality dataset.
code: krig_result <- kriging_inmet(   stations_df = rain_sf,   mun_geo     = mun_grid_sf ) #> [using ordinary kriging] mun_pred <- mun_centroid |>   select(code_muni) |>   bind_cols(     krig_result |>       st_drop_geometry() |>       select(         precip_krig     = var1.pred,         precip_krig_var = var1.var       )   )

title: Spatial Interpolation Using Ordinary Kriging
text: following map displays municipality-level rainfall estimates obtained ordinary kriging.
code: p1 <- mun_24 |>   left_join(mun_pred, by = "code_muni") |>   ggplot() +   geom_sf(aes(fill = precip_krig), color = NA) +   labs(title = "Ordinary Kriging") +   scale_fill_distiller(     palette = "RdYlGn",     direction = 1,     na.value = "grey80"   ) +   theme_void() +   theme(     legend.position = c(0.9, 0.1)   )

title: Spatial Interpolation Using Ordinary Kriging
text: comparison, map assigns municipality rainfall value closest weather station. figure compares rainfall estimates generated using ordinary kriging values obtained nearest-station approach.  Ordinary kriging generally produces smoother spatial surfaces incorporates information multiple nearby stations, whereas nearest-station method assigns value municipalities linked given station may introduce abrupt spatial discontinuities. approach advantages limitations: Ordinary kriging accounts spatial dependence usually produces realistic spatial patterns. However, statistical interpolation method, can produce physically impossible values (negative rainfall) tends smooth surface, high rainfall totals may underestimated. Nearest station preserves observed values, including extremes. However, many municipalities may share station, creates large areas identical values artificial boundaries neighboring municipalities. Real rainfall change abruptly boundaries. histograms compare distribution municipality-level estimates approaches.
code: data("inmet_stations")  mun_stations2 <- mun_stations |>    left_join(inmet_stations |> select(code_wmo, creation_year)) |>    filter(creation_year <= 2024) |>    arrange(distance) |>    distinct(code_ibge7, .keep_all = TRUE)  mun_floods <- floods_rs |>   left_join(     mun_stations2,     by = c("code_wmo" = "code_wmo")   )  p2 <- mun_24 |>   left_join(     mun_floods |>       select(code_ibge7, total_rainfall),     by = c("code_muni" = "code_ibge7")   ) |>   ggplot() +   geom_sf(aes(fill = total_rainfall), color = NA) +   labs(title = "Nearest Station") +   scale_fill_distiller(     palette = "RdYlGn",     direction = 1,     na.value = "grey80"   ) +   theme_void() +   theme(     legend.position = c(0.9, 0.1)   )

what: Example: Maximum temperature in Rio de Janeiro state (2026)
title: Download Weather, Natural Disaster, and Fire Hotspot Data from Brazil
text: First, download historical INMET CSV files download_inmet(). Next, convert raw files partitioned Apache Arrow dataset build_inmet_dataset(). step essential: station’s CSV file 8,000 rows per year, 500 stations Brazil, single year can reach 4 million observations. much computers handle efficiently plain CSV files. Finally, use read_inmet() query processed dataset.
code: library(climateBR) library(dplyr) data("mun_stations")  # The package includes datasets that speed up data aggregation. # For example, `mun_stations` was created with `nearest_stations()` and links # each of Brazil's 5,570 municipalities to its five nearest stations.  download_inmet(   years = 2026,   unzip_to = "data/raw/inmet" )  build_inmet_dataset(   input = "data/raw/inmet/",   output = "data/processed/inmet/" )  df_inmet <- read_inmet(path = "data/processed/inmet")  temp_rj <- df_inmet |>    group_by(ano, mes, codigo_wmo) |>    summarise(     temp_max = max(       temperatura_maxima_na_hora_ant_aut_c,       na.rm = TRUE     )   ) |>    left_join(     mun_stations |>        filter(station_order == 1) |>        select(state_muni, code_ibge7, code_wmo),      by = c("codigo_wmo" = "code_wmo")   ) |>    filter(state_muni == "RJ") |>    collect() |>    filter(is.finite(temp_max)) |> # drop station-months with no readings   arrange(-temp_max)    # A tibble: 644 × 6 # # Groups:   ano, mes [7] #      ano   mes codigo_wmo temp_max state_muni code_ibge7 #    <int> <int> <chr>         <dbl> <chr>           <dbl> #  1  2026     1 A601           41   RJ            3305554 #  2  2026     1 A601           41   RJ            3304144 #  3  2026     1 A601           41   RJ            3303609 #  4  2026     1 A601           41   RJ            3302270 #  5  2026     1 A601           41   RJ            3302007 #  6  2026     1 A621           40.8 RJ            3305109 #  7  2026     1 A621           40.8 RJ            3303500 #  8  2026     1 A621           40.8 RJ            3303203 #  9  2026     1 A621           40.8 RJ            3302858 # 10  2026     1 A621           40.8 RJ            3300456 # # ℹ 634 more rows # # ℹ Use `print(n = ...)` to see more rows library(ggplot2)  temp_rj |>    ggplot(aes(x = as.character(mes), y = temp_max)) +   geom_boxplot() +   theme_linedraw() +   labs(y = "Max. temp. (°C)", x = "Month") library(geobr)  mun_24 <- geobr::read_municipality(year = 2024)  mun_rj <- mun_24 |>    filter(abbrev_state == "RJ") |>    select(code_muni, geom)  # `temp_rj` already has one row per municipality and month mun_temp_rj <- mun_rj |>    left_join(     temp_rj,      by = c("code_muni" = "code_ibge7")   )  mun_temp_rj$mes <- factor(   mun_temp_rj$mes,   levels = 1:12,   labels = month.name )  ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = mun_temp_rj, aes(fill = temp_max)) +   scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdYlGn") +   facet_wrap(.~mes) +   labs(fill = "Max. temp. (°C)") +   theme_void() +   theme(     legend.position = c(0.785, 0.185),     plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white")   )

title: Download Weather, Natural Disaster, and Fire Hotspot Data from Brazil
code: library(climateBR) library(tidyverse) library(sf)  apac <- download_apac(years = 2026) data("apac_stations")  apac_flood <- apac |>   filter(`Mês/Ano` == "mai/2026") |>   mutate(     code_apac     = as.character(`Código`)   ) |>   select(code_apac, chuva_maio_01 = `01`) |>    filter(!is.na(chuva_maio_01)) |>   inner_join(     apac_stations |> select(code_apac, station_name, code_ibge7, lat, lon),     by = "code_apac"   ) |>   filter(!is.na(lat), code_ibge7 != 2605459) |>   distinct(lat, lon, .keep_all = TRUE)  apac_flood_sf <- apac_flood |>   st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)  mun_pe <- geobr::read_municipality(code_muni = "PE", year = 2024) |>   filter(code_muni != 2605459) |>   select(code_muni, geom) |>   st_transform(crs = 4326)  krig_pe <- kriging_inmet(   stations_df = apac_flood_sf,   mun_geo     = st_centroid(mun_pe),   var         = "chuva_maio_01" )  mun_rain_pe <- mun_pe |>   mutate(chuva_krig = pmax(krig_pe$var1.pred, 0))  ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = mun_rain_pe, aes(fill = chuva_krig), color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.1) +   scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdYlGn", direction = 1) +   labs(fill = "Rainfall (mm)\nMay 1, 2026") +   theme_void() +   theme(     legend.position = "bottom",     legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm"),     plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)   )
